g.text: 41 bits timestamp | 10 bits machine ID | 12 bits sequence (resets every ms)
63 bits used of 64 -- concatenated left to right, then read as one integer
Same millisecond, two machines -- no collision
Identical timestamp, but the machine-ID field differs -> the final 64-bit IDs are guaranteed different.
10 bits machine ID -> max 1,024 concurrently-registered machines.
12 bits sequence -> max 4,096 IDs/ms per machine (4.096M/sec/machine) before stalling for the next tick.
41 bits timestamp -> ~69 years of range from a custom epoch before the field overflows.
